title: Introduction to Isotropy Subgroups and Displacive Phase Transitions
opening_text:
Introduction to
               Isotropy Subgroups and Displacive Phase Transitions
                          Harold T. Stokes and Dorian M. Hatch
                          Brigham Young University, Provo, Utah
                                       April 2006


This is an introduction to the concepts of isotropy subgroups and how they are applied
to the description of displacive phase transitions. We try to use a physically intuitive
approach here. We begin with atomic displacements in a crystal, then show how the
application of symmetry leads to the concepts of irreducible representations and finally
isotropy subgroups. This paper is divided into two parts, theory and examples. They
should be read in parallel. The theoretical principles explained in part 1
